clinician.final_diagnosis: grade III hemangiopericytoma according to the WHO 2016 classification
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old male presented with one month of progressively intense, analgesic-resistant headaches and normal neurological examination. Brain MRI with gadolinium (E001) revealed a left temporo-parieto-occipital intraaxial tumor causing sub-falcoial and temporal engagement, initially interpreted as a high-grade glial tumor. The patient underwent craniotomy and tumor excision, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy using VMAT technique to a total dose of 54Gy with good tolerance (E003). The final histopathological diagnosis established grade III hemangiopericytoma (WHO 2016), distinct from the initially suspected high-grade glioma.
